text_blocks.snippet: A COVID swab test, also known as a nasal swab test, is a common method for detecting the presence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes COVID-19. These tests involve inserting a swab into the nasal cavity to collect a sample, which is then analyzed for viral genetic material or antigens.

list.title: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) Tests:
list.snippet: These lab-based tests amplify the virus's genetic material, making it easier to detect, according to the Cleveland Clinic. PCR tests are highly sensitive and considered the gold standard for COVID-19 diagnosis.

list.title: Antigen Tests:
list.snippet: These tests detect specific proteins (antigens) on the surface of the virus. Antigen tests are generally faster and more readily available than PCR tests, but they may be less sensitive, particularly for detecting low levels of the virus according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov).
